mainTopic: The time limits of the חמץ prohibitions, the sources for the מצה obligation, and whose view the משנה follows
overview: This עמוד finishes a ברייתא about when the איסור חמץ applies. רבי שמעון says there is a Torah prohibition only during פסח, while the clause forbidding הנאה reflects the תנא קמא (רבי יהודה). רבי יוסי הגלילי is amazed that anyone forbids benefit from חמץ at all. A second ברייתא records a dispute. רבי יהודה learns from 'לא תאכל עליו חמץ' that eating חמץ from midday on ערב פסח breaks a לאו. רבי שמעון ties the חמץ ban to the time of the מצוה of eating מצה. The גמרא then shows how each תנא uses the three פסוקים about חמץ, and where each one learns that מצה is a חובה even nowadays. It also shows how each learns that a טמא or a traveler must still eat מצה and מרור. Finally, the גמרא asks whose view our משנה follows and rules out רבי יהודה. It begins to test רבי שמעון, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: no Torah prohibition on חמץ before or after פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון rules that חמץ before its time and after its time carries no prohibition at all. During פסח it carries כרת and a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: חמץ before its time and after its time, one does not transgress anything with it. During its time, one transgresses with it a כרת and a negative commandment.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא presents רבי שמעון's view of when the איסור חמץ applies. In his view it applies only during פסח itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Before its time' means ערב פסח from midday on, and 'after its time' means after פסח ends. רבי שמעון says there is no Torah prohibition at all in those windows ('בלא כלום'). Only during the seven days is there both כרת and a לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: Before its time: ערב פסח from midday on
After its time: after פסח is over
During its time: the seven days of פסח
With nothing at all, meaning no prohibition
Spiritual cutting-off, the punishment for eating חמץ on פסח

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Chametz before its time and after its time,
one does not transgress anything with it.
phrases.notes: No Torah prohibition at all

phrases.english: During its time,
one transgresses with it a karet and a negative commandment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from earlier on the דף, giving רבי שמעון's view after the תנא קמא (רבי יהודה).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Torah prohibition of חמץ applies only during פסח, with כרת and a לאו. Before and after פסח there is no prohibition.

steps.title: The clause about benefit belongs to the תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that from when eating is forbidden, benefit is forbidden too. The גמרא comments that this clause returns to the view of the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And from the time that it is forbidden to eat, it is forbidden for benefit.' Here we have come back to the תנא קמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that this line does not fit רבי שמעון. It explains that the line actually states the view of the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The clause 'from when eating is forbidden' assumes eating is already forbidden from midday on ערב פסח. רבי שמעון just said nothing is forbidden then. So the line must reflect רבי יהודה, the תנא קמא, who does forbid חמץ before its time.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition on eating
A prohibition on deriving any benefit
We have come back to the first Tanna's view

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this line as רבי שמעון's words just because it comes right after him. The גמרא tells us it belongs to the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: And from the time that it is forbidden to eat,
it is forbidden for benefit.
We have come back to the first Tanna.
phrases.notes: This is the גמרא's own remark.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves an implied contradiction between this clause and רבי שמעון's ruling in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reattribution of a clause to a different Tanna
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The clause seems to continue רבי שמעון's words.
steps.terutzMaskana: The clause expresses the view of the תנא קמא (רבי יהודה), who forbids חמץ from midday on ערב פסח.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי is amazed that benefit is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי expresses amazement at the idea that one may not benefit from חמץ during all seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: Be astonished at yourself. How can חמץ be forbidden for benefit all seven days!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי הגלילי disagrees with everyone above. He holds that חמץ is forbidden only for eating, not for benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier views all assume an אסור הנאה on חמץ. רבי יוסי הגלילי rejects that assumption with strong language. His textual source is explained later on the דף.

keyTerms.meaning: Be astonished at yourself, an expression of strong surprise
All seven days of פסח

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
Be astonished at yourself,

phrases.aramaic: הֵיאַךְ חָמֵץ אָסוּר בַּהֲנָאָה כׇּל שִׁבְעָה!
phrases.english: how can chametz be forbidden for benefit all seven days!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion that rejects the אסור הנאה assumed in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חמץ on פסח is forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a separate debate about הנאה from חמץ, which the גמרא examines later.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: eating חמץ from midday breaks a לאו
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי יהודה's view: eating חמץ after six hours (midday) on ערב פסח violates a לאו, learned from 'לא תאכל עליו חמץ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that one who eats חמץ from six hours onward transgresses a negative commandment? As it says: 'You shall not eat חמץ with it.' These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא opens. רבי יהודה brings a פסוק to show there is a Torah לאו on eating חמץ from midday on ערב פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'עליו' ('with it') refers to the קרבן פסח, which is slaughtered from midday on the fourteenth. So in רבי יהודה's reading, the ban on חמץ starts as soon as the קרבן פסח can be brought. This is the source for his 'before its time' prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
From six hours onward, meaning after midday
A negative commandment (לאו)
With it, referring here to the קרבן פסח

phrases.english: And from where do we know that one who eats chametz
from six hours onward
transgresses a negative commandment?
As it says: 'You shall not eat chametz with it.'
phrases.notes: דברים ט״ז:ג

phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן לָאוֹכֵל חָמֵץ מִשֵּׁשׁ שָׁעוֹת וּלְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא that supplies the textual source for the 'before its time' prohibition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating חמץ from midday on ערב פסח violates a לאו, based on 'לא תאכל עליו חמץ'.

steps.title: רבי שמעון challenges רבי יהודה from the rest of the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון objects that the same פסוק goes on to say 'seven days you shall eat מצות עליו'. That continuation shows 'עליו' cannot mean from the time of the קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said to him: Is it possible to say so? Doesn't it already say: 'You shall not eat חמץ with it; seven days you shall eat מצות with it'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון attacks רבי יהודה's reading by quoting the full פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'עליו' meant 'from when the קרבן פסח is slaughtered', then the second half of the פסוק would require eating מצה on the fourteenth as well. No one holds that. So 'עליו' cannot carry the meaning רבי יהודה gives it.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it possible to say so?
Doesn't it already say?
Matzos

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said to him:
Is it possible to say so?
Doesn't it already say:
'You shall not eat chametz with it;
seven days you shall eat matzos with it'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks רבי יהודה's derivation from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's reading of 'עליו' as the time of the קרבן פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same 'עליו' is attached to eating מצה. Reading it as the time of the קרבן פסח would wrongly require eating מצה on the fourteenth.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the לאו of חמץ is tied to the מצוה of מצה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון offers his own reading. The פסוק links the two halves, so the לאו of חמץ applies only when the מצוה of eating מצה applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does the פסוק teach with 'You shall not eat חמץ with it'? At a time when he is obligated to get up and eat מצה, he is subject to 'do not eat חמץ'. At a time when he is not obligated to get up and eat מצה, he is not subject to 'do not eat חמץ'.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רבי יהודה's reading, רבי שמעון explains what the פסוק really teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two halves of the פסוק are placed side by side to teach that they run on the same schedule. The מצוה of eating מצה starts on the night of the fifteenth, so the לאו of eating חמץ starts then too. On ערב פסח after midday there is no מצה obligation, so there is no לאו either. This matches רבי שמעון's ruling in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the verse come to teach?
The positive command to get up and eat מצה
The prohibition against eating חמץ
He is subject to it; it applies to him

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, the לאו of eating חמץ and the מצוה of eating מצה go together. No מצה obligation means no חמץ לאו.

phrases.english: If so, what does the verse teach with
'You shall not eat chametz with it'?
At a time when he is obligated to get up and eat matzah,
he is subject to 'do not eat chametz';
and at a time when he is not obligated to get up and eat matzah,
he is not subject to 'do not eat chametz'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge in step 5, רבי שמעון supplies his own reading of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The לאו of eating חמץ applies only when the מצוה of eating מצה applies, so not on ערב פסח.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי יהודה's source, since his reading of 'עליו' was just challenged.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next move by asking how רבי יהודה supports his view of three time periods for the חמץ prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה, the תנא קמא, holds that a לאו applies to חמץ before פסח, during it, and after it. רבי שמעון holds that it applies only during פסח. The גמרא now asks for the scriptural basis of רבי יהודה's three-period view; the next step answers.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the two ברייתות are quoted, the גמרא asks for the source of רבי יהודה's view that חמץ is forbidden before, during, and after פסח.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for רבי יהודה's view that a לאו applies before, during, and after פסח.

steps.title: Three verses for three time periods
steps.stepSummary: Three separate פסוקים forbid eating חמץ. רבי יהודה assigns one to before פסח, one to after פסח, and one to during פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three פסוקים are written: 'חמץ shall not be eaten,' 'And any leavened thing you shall not eat,' and 'You shall not eat חמץ with it.' One is for before its time, one is for after its time, and one is for during its time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה sees three repeated prohibitions in the Torah. Each one must teach something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the Torah would not repeat the same ban without reason, each פסוק covers a different period. One covers before פסח (midday on ערב פסח), one covers after פסח (חמץ owned during פסח), and one covers פסח itself. This explains why רבי יהודה holds a לאו applies in all three periods, unlike רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Three verses
Are written
Anything leavened
One

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: there is a לאו before, during, and after פסח, learned from three פסוקים. רבי שמעון: there is a Torah prohibition only during פסח, tied to the מצוה of מצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the textual root of the dispute over חמץ on ערב פסח and חמץ that was owned during פסח, which the גמרא continues to develop.

phrases.english: Three verses are written:
'Chametz shall not be eaten,'
phrases.notes: שמות י״ג:ג

phrases.english: 'And any leavened thing you shall not eat,'
phrases.notes: שמות י״ב:כ

phrases.english: 'You shall not eat chametz with it.'
phrases.notes: דברים ט״ז:ג

phrases.english: One is for before its time,
and one is for after its time,
and one is for during its time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three פסוקים forbid eating חמץ. Each one covers a different time: before פסח, after פסח, and during פסח.

steps.title: How רבי שמעון uses the three פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון uses one פסוק for the prohibition during פסח itself. He uses 'וכל מחמצת' to teach that חמץ made leavened by another substance is also forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does רבי שמעון use the three פסוקים? One is for the prohibition during its time, meaning during פסח. 'And all that is leavened' is needed for what a ברייתא teaches: I would only know that dough that became חמץ on its own is forbidden. How do I know that dough which became חמץ because of another substance is also forbidden? The פסוק says: 'All that is leavened you shall not eat.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי שמעון uses the three פסוקים, since he does not need them for three time periods the way רבי יהודה does. It answers by assigning two of them so far.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון forbids חמץ only during פסח, so only one פסוק is needed for timing. The other פסוקים must teach something else. The words 'כל מחמצת' teach that חמץ is forbidden no matter how it became leavened, even if something else (like yeast or sourdough) caused it.

keyTerms.meaning: During its own time, meaning the seven days of פסח
Something leavened (the word used in the פסוק)
Became חמץ on its own, by its natural process
Because of another substance, such as yeast or sourdough
The פסוק teaches us (introduces the source)

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'ורבי שמעון' is only two words long, but it is a full question: 'What does רבי שמעון do with the three פסוקים?' The rest of this step is the answer.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon, what does he do with the three verses?
phrases.notes: The גמרא just says 'And רבי שמעון?' and leaves the rest of the question for you to fill in.

phrases.english: One verse is for the prohibition during its time.
phrases.notes: During the seven days of פסח

phrases.english: "And all that is leavened" he needs for what was taught in a baraita:
I only know about dough that became leavened on its own.
From where do I know about dough leavened because of another substance?
The verse says: "All that is leavened you shall not eat."
phrases.notes: The word 'כל' (all) includes every kind of leavening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After seeing how רבי יהודה uses the three פסוקים, the גמרא turns to רבי שמעון.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי שמעון learns from the three פסוקים, since he needs only one for timing.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One פסוק is for during פסח. 'וכל מחמצת' teaches that חמץ made by another substance is forbidden.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's third פסוק: פסח מצרים had only one day of חמץ
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון uses 'לא יאכל חמץ' for רבי יוסי הגלילי's teaching. In פסח מצרים, the prohibition of חמץ lasted only one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'חמץ shall not be eaten' he needs for what a ברייתא teaches. רבי יוסי הגלילי says: How do we know that in the פסח of Egypt, the prohibition of חמץ lasted only one day? The פסוק says 'חמץ shall not be eaten,' and right next to it: 'Today you are going out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining רבי שמעון's use of the three פסוקים by assigning the third one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'לא יאכל חמץ' is placed right next to 'היום אתם יוצאים' (today you are leaving). That closeness teaches that in Egypt, חמץ was forbidden only on that one day. So all three פסוקים are now used up for רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: The very first פסח, celebrated in Egypt at the time of the Exodus
Its prohibition of חמץ
Applies, is in effect
It is placed right next to it (in the Torah)

phrases.english: "Leavened bread shall not be eaten" he needs for what was taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
From where do we know about the Passover in Egypt

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין חִימּוּצוֹ נוֹהֵג אֶלָּא יוֹם אֶחָד?
phrases.english: that its prohibition of leaven applied only one day?
The verse says: "Leavened bread shall not be eaten,"
and right next to it: "Today you are going out."
phrases.notes: שמות יג:ג-ד

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יֵאָכֵל חָמֵץ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of how רבי שמעון uses the three פסוקים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The third פסוק teaches רבי יוסי הגלילי's rule that חמץ in Egypt was forbidden for only one day.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון: one פסוק is for during פסח, 'וכל מחמצת' is for leavening by another substance, and 'לא יאכל חמץ' is for פסח מצרים lasting one day.

steps.title: Where does רבי יהודה learn about leavening by another substance?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה used all three פסוקים for time periods. So where does he learn that חמץ caused by another substance is forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה: from where does he know that dough leavened because of another substance is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about רבי יהודה. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון learned this rule from 'וכל מחמצת'. But רבי יהודה already used that פסוק for one of his three time periods, so he seems to have no source left for this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda,
from where does he know about leavening due to another substance?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, מֵחֲמַת דָּבָר אַחֵר מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבי שמעון's use of 'וכל מחמצת' back onto רבי יהודה, who used that פסוק differently.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יהודה's source for the rule that חמץ caused by another substance is forbidden.

steps.title: רבי יהודה learns it from the word 'מחמצת' itself
steps.stepSummary: The Torah chose the word 'מחמצת', which already includes leavening by another substance.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the fact that the Torah expressed it with the word 'מחמצת'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. רבי יהודה does not need an extra word, because the word 'מחמצת' itself teaches the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The form 'מחמצת' implies something that was made leavened, which covers dough leavened by an outside agent. רבי שמעון needed the word 'כל' to include this case. רבי יהודה finds it in the basic word, so the פסוק remains free for his time-period teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Expressed it, put it in these words
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳
With the wording of

phrases.english: From the fact that the Merciful One expressed it
with the term "that which is leavened."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'מחמצת' by itself includes leavening caused by another substance.

steps.title: Where does רבי יהודה get רבי יוסי הגלילי's teaching?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה used 'לא יאכל חמץ' for a time period. So where does he learn that פסח מצרים had only one day of חמץ?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the teaching of רבי יוסי הגלילי, from where does רבי יהודה know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a second question about רבי יהודה. Two answers follow in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון learned רבי יוסי הגלילי's rule from 'לא יאכל חמץ'. רבי יהודה already used that פסוק for one of his time periods, so the גמרא asks where he gets this rule.

phrases.english: The teaching of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, from where does he know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 11, now about the third פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יהודה's source for the rule that חמץ in פסח מצרים was forbidden for only one day.

steps.title: First answer: from the nearby word 'היום'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה still learns the rule from the placement of 'היום' next to the פסוק, even though he uses the פסוק itself for a time period.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: he learns it from the fact that 'today' is placed next to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer. רבי יהודה learns from the same closeness of פסוקים that רבי יוסי הגלילי uses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לא יאכל חמץ' teach רבי יהודה an extra time period. The placement of 'היום' right next to them is a separate hint, and it teaches the one-day rule for Egypt. So one פסוק gives two teachings.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces one of two possible answers)

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
from the fact that "today" is placed next to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: מִדִּסְמִיךְ לֵיהּ הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The closeness of 'היום' teaches the one-day rule, apart from the main meaning of the פסוק.

steps.title: Second answer: רבי יהודה does not learn from סמוכין
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה does not learn from the placement of פסוקים next to each other. So he does not accept רבי יוסי הגלילי's teaching at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: he does not learn from juxtaposed פסוקים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. רבי יהודה simply does not hold of this teaching, so he needs no source for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי's rule depends on סמוכין, learning from פסוקים placed next to each other. רבי יהודה generally does not use that method (except in limited cases). So for him there is no one-day rule, and חמץ in Egypt was forbidden for all seven days.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning a law from two פסוקים placed next to each other
He does not expound, does not learn from

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not give רבי יהודה a different source. It says he rejects רבי יוסי הגלילי's teaching altogether, so no source is needed.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה learns leavening by another substance from the word 'מחמצת' itself. For the one-day rule of פסח מצרים, he either learns it from the nearby word 'היום', or he rejects it because he does not learn from סמוכין.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
he does not expound juxtaposed verses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: סְמוּכִין לָא דָּרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative answer to step 13, replacing the approach of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה does not learn from סמוכין, so he rejects רבי יוסי הגלילי's teaching altogether.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: eating חמץ after six hours is a לאו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: רבי יהודה learns from 'לא תאכל עליו חמץ' that eating חמץ from midday on ערב פסח breaks a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: From where do we know that someone who eats חמץ after six hours (midday) breaks a negative commandment? The פסוק says: 'You shall not eat חמץ with it.' These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a ברייתא it quoted earlier so it can analyze it more closely. רבי יהודה says the לאו against חמץ already starts at midday on ערב פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עליו' means 'with it', meaning with the קרבן פסח. The פסח is slaughtered from midday on, so רבי יהודה reads the פסוק as saying: from the time the פסח can be brought, you may not eat חמץ. This makes the six-hour prohibition a real Torah לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: From six hours onward, meaning from midday on ערב פסח
A negative commandment (לאו)
'With it', here understood as with the קרבן פסח

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is going back to quote the ברייתא from before.

phrases.english: And from where do we know regarding one who eats חמץ
from six hours and onward
that he transgresses a negative commandment?
As it is said: 'You shall not eat חמץ with it'
phrases.notes: דברים 16:3; 'with it' means with the קרבן פסח

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא to analyze the debate between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, eating חמץ from midday on ערב פסח breaks a לאו, learned from 'לא תאכל עליו חמץ'.

steps.title: רבי שמעון objects: the פסוק links עליו to the seven days
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון challenges רבי יהודה: the same פסוק goes on to say 'seven days you shall eat מצות with it', so 'עליו' points to the days of פסח, not to ערב פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said to him: Can you really say that? The Torah already says: 'You shall not eat חמץ with it; seven days you shall eat מצות with it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון attacks רבי יהודה's reading of the פסוק. He reads the whole פסוק together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the full פסוק, 'עליו' appears twice: no חמץ 'עליו', and מצות 'עליו' for seven days. So the ban on חמץ is tied to the time when you eat מצה, which is the seven days of פסח. That leaves no Torah לאו before פסח starts.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is it possible to say so?', a sharp objection
'But isn't it already stated', introducing a counter-פסוק
Seven days, the days of פסח itself

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said to him:
Is it possible to say so?
Isn't it already stated:
'You shall not eat חמץ with it;
seven days you shall eat מצות with it.'
phrases.notes: The ban on חמץ is paired with the time of eating מצה

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר כֵּן? וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to רבי יהודה's reading in step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's use of 'לא תאכל עליו חמץ' for the time from midday on ערב פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק itself links 'עליו' to the seven days of מצה, so it cannot be talking about ערב פסח.

steps.title: Isn't רבי שמעון right?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה deals with רבי שמעון's strong point.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for רבי יהודה: isn't רבי שמעון speaking well to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא itself agrees that רבי שמעון's objection looks strong. It sets up the next step, where it will explain רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה must explain why the end of the פסוק ('seven days you shall eat מצות') does not cancel his reading of the beginning. The גמרא wants to know what job he gives to that second half.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He is saying well', meaning the argument is strong

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, שַׁפִּיר קָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן?
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda: isn't Rabbi Shimon speaking well to him?
phrases.notes: So how does רבי יהודה answer?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, שַׁפִּיר קָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presses רבי שמעון's objection against רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The combined פסוק seems to support רבי שמעון, so רבי יהודה needs a different way to read it.

steps.title: The link makes מצה an obligation even nowadays
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the pairing of חמץ and מצה in the פסוק teaches that eating מצה is a חובה even without the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה can tell you: that part of the פסוק comes to make מצה an obligation even nowadays.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יהודה's answer. The second half of the פסוק has a different job; it is not about timing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a קרבן פסח, one might think there is no longer a duty to eat מצה. The פסוק places מצה next to חמץ to teach a comparison: the ban on חמץ applies even without the בית המקדש, so the duty to eat מצה does too. So 'עליו' at the start can still refer to the time of the קרבן פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: To set it as a firm obligation
Nowadays, when there is no בית המקדש or קרבן פסח
'That is what it comes for'

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the חובה to eat מצה on the night of פסח today, even without a קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda would say to you:
that part comes to establish it as an obligation
even nowadays — that is what it comes for.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 17-18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirects the second half of the פסוק to a different lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase 'seven days you shall eat מצות with it' fixes the time of the חמץ ban.
steps.terutzMaskana: That phrase teaches that מצה is a חובה even nowadays, so it does not limit רבי יהודה's reading.

steps.title: Where does רבי שמעון learn the מצה obligation nowadays?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון uses the פסוק for timing, so where does he learn that מצה is a חובה even nowadays?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון: from where does he learn that מצה is an obligation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי שמעון. His reading of the פסוק uses it up, so he needs another source for the rule that מצה is a חובה today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides accept that מצה is a חובה even without the קרבן פסח. Since רבי שמעון reads the פסוק as a time link, the גמרא asks for his source.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where does he have it?', a request for a source

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, לְקוֹבְעוֹ חוֹבָה מְנָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon, from where does he derive establishing it as an obligation?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, לְקוֹבְעוֹ חוֹבָה מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining רבי יהודה, asks for רבי שמעון's source for the same rule
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי שמעון's source that eating מצה is a חובה even nowadays

steps.title: רבי שמעון learns it from בערב תאכלו
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learns the חובה of מצה from 'בערב תאכלו מצות', a פסוק not tied to the קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'In the evening you shall eat מצות.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון has a separate פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בערב תאכלו מצות' ties the מצה obligation to the date, the night of the fifteenth, rather than to the קרבן פסח. So it applies even when there is no קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He derives it', meaning he learns it from
'In the evening you shall eat' (שמות 12:18)

phrases.english: He derives it from 'In the evening you shall eat.'
phrases.notes: The obligation is tied to the date, not to the קרבן

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון learns the ongoing מצה obligation from 'בערב תאכלו מצות'.

steps.title: רבי יהודה uses בערב תאכלו for the טמא and the traveler
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה needs 'בערב תאכלו' to teach that someone who is טמא or on a דרך רחוקה must still eat מצה and מרור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? He needs that פסוק for someone who is טמא or was on a far-away trip. You might have thought: since he does not eat the קרבן פסח, he also does not eat מצה and מרור. So the פסוק teaches us that he does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks and answers in one line: what does רבי יהודה do with 'בערב תאכלו'? He uses it for a different rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who is טמא or far away cannot bring the קרבן פסח on time. One might think מצה and מרור are only side-dishes to the קרבן, so without it he would skip them. The פסוק teaches that he must still eat them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He needs it', meaning the פסוק is used for another lesson
Ritually impure, so unable to bring the קרבן פסח
A far-away trip, so unable to reach the בית המקדש in time
'You might have thought', introducing a mistaken assumption
'It teaches us', the פסוק corrects that mistake

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda? He needs it
for one who is impure or who was on a distant journey.
It would enter your mind to say:
since he does not eat the Pesach offering —
he should not eat מצה and מרור either.
It teaches us that he does.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְטָמֵא וְשֶׁהָיָה בְּדֶרֶךְ רְחוֹקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי יהודה does not use 'בערב תאכלו' for the nowadays obligation
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה uses 'בערב תאכלו' to obligate a טמא or traveler in מצה and מרור.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: no פסוק is needed for the טמא and traveler
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the טמא and the traveler obviously eat מצה and מרור, because they are no worse than an ערל or a בן נכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון? For the טמא and the one on a far-away trip, no פסוק is needed, because they are no worse than an ערל and a בן נכר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי שמעון gets the rule about the טמא and traveler without 'בערב תאכלו'. It is a logical argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ערל and a בן נכר are barred from the קרבן פסח for more serious reasons, yet they still eat מצה and מרור. A טמא or traveler, who is held back only by circumstance, is surely no worse. So a separate פסוק is unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: 'No פסוק is needed'
'Is not worse than'
An uncircumcised man, barred from the קרבן פסח
An outsider or estranged person, barred from the קרבן פסח

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, טָמֵא וְשֶׁהָיָה בְּדֶרֶךְ רְחוֹקָה
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon: for one impure or on a distant journey
a verse is not needed,
since he is no worse than an uncircumcised man or a בן נכר.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, טָמֵא וְשֶׁהָיָה בְּדֶרֶךְ רְחוֹקָה לָא אִיצְטְרִיךְ קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי שמעון is free to use 'בערב תאכלו' for the nowadays obligation
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The טמא and the traveler are no worse than an ערל or בן נכר, who eat מצה and מרור, so no פסוק is needed.

steps.title: Proof from 'בו': the ערל still eats מצה and מרור
steps.stepSummary: The word 'בו' in 'וכל ערל לא יאכל בו' limits the ban to the קרבן פסח, so the ערל still eats מצה and מרור.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And no ערל shall eat of it.' Of it, the קרבן פסח, he does not eat. But he does eat מצה and מרור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the claim from step 23 that an ערל eats מצה and מרור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'בו' ('of it') tells us the ban covers only the קרבן פסח itself. That shows the ערל keeps the מצה and מרור obligation, which is the basis for the argument about the טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Of it', which limits the ban to the קרבן פסח alone
'As it is written'

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And no uncircumcised man shall eat of it' —
phrases.notes: שמות 12:48

phrases.english: of it he does not eat,
but he does eat מצה and מרור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי שמעון's argument in step 23
steps.raayaObject: That an ערל, though barred from the קרבן פסח, still eats מצה and מרור
steps.raayaSupportSource: The limiting word 'בו' in 'וכל ערל לא יאכל בו'

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the Torah wrote it in both places
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers that even if the rule could be learned from the ערל, the Torah chose to write it in both places.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? It is written about this one, and it is written about that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יהודה's reply to רבי שמעון's argument that no פסוק is needed. This closes the back-and-forth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה accepts that the rule might follow from the ערל. Even so, the Torah wrote it explicitly for both cases: the ערל and בן נכר through 'בו', and the טמא and traveler through 'בערב תאכלו'. So he can still read 'בערב תאכלו' this way and learn the nowadays obligation from the pairing of חמץ and מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is written in this and written in that', meaning the Torah states it in both places

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that מצה is a חובה even nowadays and that a טמא or traveler eats מצה and מרור. They disagree on the sources, and on whether there is a לאו from midday on ערב פסח. רבי יהודה: 'לא תאכל עליו חמץ' gives the six-hour לאו, its pairing with מצה gives the nowadays obligation, and 'בערב תאכלו' covers the טמא. רבי שמעון: there is no six-hour לאו, because the פסוק ties the חמץ ban to the seven days of מצה. 'בערב תאכלו' gives the nowadays obligation, and the טמא is learned from the ערל.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda?
It is written in this case, and it is written in that case.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: כְּתִיב בְּהַאי וּכְתִיב בְּהַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי שמעון's argument in steps 23-24 on behalf of רבי יהודה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts that the rule is learnable, but says the Torah wrote it in both places anyway
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the טמא's rule follows from the ערל, רבי יהודה should not need 'בערב תאכלו' for it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah wrote the rule in both places, so רבי יהודה's reading of 'בערב תאכלו' stands.

steps.title: Whose opinion is our משנה?
steps.stepSummary: Having laid out the views of the תנאים, the גמרא asks which of them is the author of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does our משנה follow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא wrote our משנה. This question sets up a test of each opinion, one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה makes a split ruling: a נכרי's חמץ that stayed over פסח is permitted for benefit, but a Jew's is forbidden. The גמרא now checks which of the three views it has explained can fit this split.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? (Aramaic for 'whose view is this')
Our משנה

phrases.english: Whose opinion is our Mishnah?
phrases.notes: This is the usual way the גמרא asks who said a משנה that doesn't give a name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the opinions now explained, the גמרא returns to the משנה to find its author.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא (רבי יהודה, רבי שמעון, or רבי יוסי הגלילי) fits the משנה's split between a נכרי's חמץ and a Jew's חמץ.

steps.title: The משנה cannot follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה forbids חמץ after פסח without any limit, so he would forbid even a נכרי's חמץ. That contradicts the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is רבי יהודה, that cannot be. He spoke about חמץ in general, which includes even the חמץ of a non-Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out רבי יהודה as the author and rejects him. His ruling would forbid even a נכרי's חמץ, but the משנה permits it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said that חמץ which stayed over פסח is forbidden, and he did not say whose חמץ he meant. Since he made no exception, his ban covers a נכרי's חמץ too. The משנה clearly permits a נכרי's חמץ, so רבי יהודה cannot be its author.

keyTerms.meaning: Without any limit or detail (unqualified)
He is saying
Of a non-Jew

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה never mentioned a נכרי directly. The גמרא reads his silence as including everyone: because he spoke about חמץ without limits, it covers all חמץ.

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Yehuda —
phrases.notes: The גמרא tries out the first possibility.

phrases.english: he spoke of leavened bread without qualification,
phrases.notes: His ruling about חמץ after פסח did not say whose חמץ.

phrases.english: meaning even that of a gentile.
phrases.notes: So he would forbid a נכרי's חמץ, unlike the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question 'whose opinion is the משנה?'
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי יהודה is the author of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה's unqualified ban covers a נכרי's חמץ. The משנה permits a נכרי's חמץ. So the two conflict.

steps.title: Turning to test רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to test רבי שמעון as the author. The problem with his view comes on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it is רבי שמעון —
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא moves to the next candidate, רבי שמעון, and is about to show a difficulty with him as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With רבי יהודה ruled out, the גמרא checks whether רבי שמעון's view fits the משנה's split ruling. The sentence stops in the middle here. The actual objection to רבי שמעון comes at the start of the next passage.

keyTerms.meaning: And if
